name: Every Nonempty Passive Shore Contains an Active Root
statement: In a two-connected terminal ample interval of order at most eleven, the active lower slice $L$ is nonempty, and every nonempty passive shore $S_z$ contains some $d$ for which $L\cup\{d\}$ is ample.
proof: If $L$ were empty, every residual concept would be an active root. The passive Helly theorem would give a common owner of all nonempty shores, while the passive-root cover applied to that owner would require a shore omitting it, a contradiction. Thus $L$ is nonempty. For a nonempty $S_z$, the corresponding opposite active section $M_z$ meets $L$. The nested ample pair $L\cap M_z\subsetneq (B\cap M_z)$ lives on at most five coordinates, so relative peeling supplies a first point $p\in S_z$. The expansion-separator augmentation lemma lifts this first relative addition from the intersection to $L$, proving $L\cup\{p\}$ ample.
